summary: Allocator credit leak tied to ephemeral-log-collector fanout causing reserved pool p99 latency spiral
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 09:10 UTC BrightAssist reported sustained p99/p95 latency spikes on their reserved capacity pool. Impact: customer-experiencing degraded inference throughput and timeouts for short streamed requests. Environment: dedicated pool (reserved), us-east, tenant=brightassist-prod.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Send many short streaming requests at ~300 RPS with idle keepalive 30s. 2) Deploy customer-side telemetry sidecar that collects and forwards debug logs (ephemeral-log-collector). 3) Observe allocator credit metric and GPU attach success rate.

Observed behavior: Gradual climb in allocator-credit-debt metric (credits not released for ephemeral connections). Short-lived sidecar connections spike file descriptor and connection fanout; allocator registers attachments but credits never return quickly causing a reserved-pool attach deficit. Autoscaler does not immediately allocate extra GPUs due to short-window smoothing -> p99 latency spiral and some 5xx for queued requests.

Expected behavior: Ephemeral log collectors should not cause allocator credit leak or cause connector fanout that prevents quick credit recycle; autoscaler should react before p99 climbs beyond SLO.

Initial logs/links: metrics dashboard: https://metrics.redwood.com/d/alloc/allocator-credit?org=ops&from=2026-03-12T08:50:00Z&to=2026-03-12T09:30:00Z. Faulty sidecar logs (customer): s3://brightassist-uploads/logs/2026-03-12/collector-*.log.

Workaround applied: 2026-03-12 10:05 UTC support applied temporary throttle on sidecar ingestion at edge for brightassist-prod and bumped allocator soft-quota for their reserved pool. Early effect: allocator-credit-debt trending down and p95/p99 showed improvement within 8 minutes.

Next steps: 1) SRE to validate allocator credit accounting paths and add guard for ephemeral connection path (ticket assigned below). 2) Recommend customer disable high-frequency ephemeral collectors or switch to batched forwarding. 3) Implement rate-limiting for sidecar traffic at ingress and surface clearer telemetry. 4) Follow-up postmortem and prevention actions.
investigation_notes: 09:20 UTC - Support: correlated p99 jump with sudden increase in ephemeral connection_count for tenant brightassist-prod (connection fanout from log-collector).
09:28 UTC - SRE: allocator_credit_debt metric rose from 2% baseline to 38% over 18 minutes; attach_success_rate dipped by 14%.

09:35 UTC - Hypothesis A: ephemeral-log-collector creates large number of short-lived attach attempts; allocator allows attach but credits returned asynchronously; race/edge-case in credit return path causes leak under heavy churn.
09:41 UTC - Hypothesis B: telemetry sidecar additionally causes high tail IO causing GPU NVMe queueback -> slower attach completions and credits tied up longer than autoscaler smoothing window.
09:53 UTC - Evidence: kernel-level socket counts per node surged (node-42 and node-43); netstat and conntrack logs attached to confluence.

10:05 UTC - Mitigation: applied throttle for sidecar ingestion at edge and increased soft-quota for allocator for brightassist reserved pool. Observed recovery in p95/p99 within 8 minutes, consistent with credit pool draining.

11:00 UTC - Repro attempt in staging: reproduced p99 climb by spawning 1k ephemeral sidecar connections per minute while keeping request payloads small. Collector pattern triggered same allocator_credit_debt behavior.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-12 09:30 UTC: Customer reported timeouts on short streams. Collected metrics and elevated to SRE. Customer can confirm they deployed a debug-forwarder sidecar yesterday for log sampling.

Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-12 09:45 UTC: Looking at allocator logs now. Seeing a steady rise in credit_debt and many short attach cycles. Suspect credits not reclaimed quickly for ephemeral connects. Increasing priority and applying temporary throttles.

BrightAssist (Customer) 2026-03-12 09:50 UTC: We rolled out a debug-forwarder yesterday; can revert quickly if needed. We're seeing increased egress to the telemetry collector; happy to disable if that helps.
Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-12 10:10 UTC: Throttle applied on ingestion for tenant brightassist-prod at edge. Also increased soft-quota. Please verify traffic — we should see latency improve.
BrightAssist (Customer) 2026-03-12 10:18 UTC: Confirming latency improved and errors reduced after throttle. We'll roll back the debug-forwarder and reconfigure to batch logs.
resolution: Workaround: throttled ephemeral log-collector ingestion at edge and temporarily raised allocator soft-quota for BrightAssist reserved pool. Immediate effect: p95/p99 improved. Long-term fix: allocator credit accounting patch to ensure credits returned promptly for short-lived attaches (PR linked). Recommend gating ephemeral collectors with a default rate-limit at ingress; update runbook to include this class of failure.
follow_up_actions: Create allocator unit test that simulates many short attach/release cycles (assigned to allocator team).
Ship PR to add idempotent credit-return path and a timeout to reconcile leaked credits (github PR linked above).
Update dedicated-pool runbook to include detection alert for allocator_credit_debt > 20% for >10 minutes and automated short-term throttle on telemetry sidecars.
Customer action: BrightAssist to reconfigure debug-forwarder to batch at 30s or use sampled tracing.
Schedule postmortem meeting with SRE, Support, and Customer for 2026-03-16 if issue fully resolved.
